findings.element: the min-width: 1280px desk query in b.css governing .b-two's grid-template-columns, .b-stick's position, and the column gap; driven at 700, 768, 900, 1000, 1100, 1152, 1279, 1280 and 1440 on owner-flight, owner-editing and desk
findings.problem: Round 5 raised this band and one third of it was fixed: .b-todayRule is now 344px at every width. The other two thirds are untouched, and I re-drove them. From 701 to 1279 .b-two still resolves to ONE track - 960px at 1152, 1068px at 1279 - and .b-stick still computes position: static, so the locked promise that at desk width the count, the date and what the day is stop scrolling is false across the 579px band most unmaximised laptop windows sit in; it computes sticky only at 1280 and up. The cost is measurable in the object the product repeats most: .b-item renders 836px wide at 1152 and 944px at 1279 against 544px at 1280 and 1440. A moment - a title, a date, a short note - is drawn at 944px on a 1279 window and 544px one pixel later, a 73 per cent swing in the measure of the product's primary row, and at 944 the title sits alone with roughly 700px of void to its right (visible in shots/approach-desk--1152x800.png). Worse, at 1152x800 and 1279x800 I counted the moments intersecting the viewport on owner-flight: zero. The owner's entire first screen is the bar, one sentence, the 79, the date, Wedding day, the today rule, Nothing is planned until 1 August, DAYS AWAY, TODAY 16 JULY and an empty rail. At 1280 it is two. The same is true of the guest desk surface. And the crossing is a cliff, not a breakpoint: at 1279 to 1280 the gutter goes 32 to 56, the track goes one to two, sticky switches on, the document shortens from 2501 to 2130 and the first moment jumps 371px up the page - all on one pixel of window width. The 1152 and 1279 frames now exist in shots/, so this is no longer invisible; it has simply not been acted on.
findings.fix: Move the reading composition off the editor's breakpoint. In b.css change the desk query from min-width: 1280px to min-width: 1000px for exactly three things - .b-two's grid-template-columns, .b-stick's position: sticky, and the 56px column-gap - and leave every editor rule on min-width: 1280px so the docked editor stays a full-width sheet below 1280 as decided. Then put a ceiling on the row so no width can stretch it: .b-measure { max-width: 668px } and .b-stick { max-width: 344px }, which fixes the 701-999 band too by holding the single column to the measure it was drawn at instead of letting it run to 1068. Gate both in interaction-check.mjs: at 1000, 1152 and 1279 assert getComputedStyle of .b-stick returns position sticky, assert .b-item's rendered width never exceeds 560px at any width in the matrix, and assert at least one .b-item intersects the viewport at 1152x800 on owner-flight and desk.

findings.element: .tl-page's justify-content: safe center against its own min-height: 0px, on states publish, day, ended, loading and unfurl (master.html:241-245)
findings.problem: Five states declare vertical centring and none of them centres. .tl-page is display: flex with justify-content: safe center and min-height: 0px, so its height is exactly its content height - 569 on ended, 454 on loading, 449 on unfurl, 630 on publish - and safe center has nothing to distribute. Every one of them renders hard against the top of the viewport with the remainder as dead ground beneath. Measured at 1440x960: ended sits 68 above and 432 below, a 6.4 to 1 ratio; loading 68 above and 547 below, 8 to 1; unfurl 157 and 647; publish 67 and 370. At 768x1024 ended is 68 and 496. The ended frame at shots/approach-ended--1440x960.png shows it plainly: a 388px card centred horizontally to the pixel and pinned to the top vertically, with 45 per cent of the screen empty under it and nothing at the bottom edge to resolve it. The craft inside the card is right - its own top and bottom insets are both 81px - which is what makes the page-level placement read as an accident rather than a decision. This is the one axis nobody checked, and it is the guest's arrival screen and the guest's failure screen.
findings.fix: Give the flex container a height to distribute and let the stage take the slack. Add to shell.css: .tl-page { min-height: 100dvh } and .tl-page > .tl-stage { margin-block: auto }, which centres the stage between the lab bar and the viewport foot without moving the bar. Re-render the five states; ended at 1440x960 should land at roughly 250 above and 250 below. Gate it in interaction-check.mjs: for each of publish, day, ended, loading and unfurl at 1440x960 and 768x1024, assert the absolute difference between the stage's bounding top and innerHeight minus its bounding bottom is 24px or less.

findings.element: .b-measureHead's margin-top against .b-who in every two-column state, measured at 1280 and 1440 on owner-flight, owner-editing, desk and print
findings.problem: Raised at round 5, not fixed - only renumbered. Both columns of the composition open with the same object: an 11px mono uppercase micro-label, same size, same weight, same tracking, same ink, first mark in its column. MARA AND FINN heads the horizon, DAYS AWAY heads the measure. They were 22px apart; the space re-key has made them 20px apart, which is the same defect on a tidier number. Driven: .b-who tops at y231 and .b-measureHead at y251 on owner-flight at both 1280 and 1440; 108 against 128 on desk; 124 against 144 on print. The cause is unchanged - the margin-top is correct on the phone, where the head follows the horizon down one column and needs air above it, and is inherited into the mediums where the grid row already supplies the top. The same label is a follower on the phone and a column head on the desk and is styled as a follower in both. Now that space is enforced at the source, this is the clearest remaining case of a value that is on the ladder and in the wrong place: it passes every gate and still tells the reader the two columns were set separately.
findings.fix: Zero it where the label heads a column instead of following one. In b.css, inside the min-width desk block (min-width: 1000px after the first finding lands), add a rule setting margin-top: 0 on .b-measureHead under [data-medium="sheet"] and [data-medium="full"]. Both labels share size and weight, so flush tops means flush baselines, the measure column lifts 20px, and the printed sheet gets 20px shorter. Assert it in interaction-check.mjs: in any state where .b-two resolves to two tracks, .b-who and .b-measureHead share a bounding-box top within 1px.

findings.element: .b-stick's top: 24px at 1280 and 1440, driven by scrolling owner-flight to y900
findings.problem: When the horizon sticks it parks 24px from the viewport top. Nothing else on the page uses 24: the field's top padding is 40, its side padding is 56, the phone medium uses 20 and 28, the sheet uses 56. So at rest the horizon's first mark sits 40 below the field edge and 56 in from its side, and the moment it sticks it jumps to 24 - a top inset tighter than any other margin in the design, against a left inset of 56. The stuck block reads as crowded to the top of the window and its optical margins stop being a pair. It is the one object that is meant to hold still and be looked at while everything else moves, so it is the one object whose margins are read longest.
findings.fix: Set .b-stick { top: 40px } in b.css so the stuck horizon holds the same top inset the field uses at rest, and the stuck state keeps the 40 over 56 relationship the page already states. Assert in interaction-check.mjs that .b-stick's computed top equals the field's computed padding-top in any state where its position computes sticky.

findings.element: the sheet medium's .b-field padding, computed 56px 56px 40px 56px on state=print, against the screen card's computed 40px 56px 56px 56px
findings.problem: The paper inverts the screen's optical weighting instead of inheriting it. The guest card on screen is 40 top, 56 bottom, 56 sides - more below than above, which is the correct optical weighting for a framed block and is why the desk card sits right. The keepsake is 56 top, 40 bottom, 56 sides - more above than below - so the printed block hangs high in the sheet and the foot and the URL line finish 40 from the paper edge against 56 of side margin. On a page held in the hand that reads as the footer crowding the bottom trim, and it is the one artifact in this product that cannot be reflowed after it exists. The A4 itself is now genuinely right - I rendered it at 794x1123 and page.pdf at A4 returns exactly one page with the horizon beside the measure at 220px and 332px - which is what makes the margin the remaining thing to look at.
findings.fix: In b.css set the sheet medium's .b-print and .b-field padding to 48px 56px 64px so the printed block carries more below than above in the same 40-to-56 proportion the screen card uses, and re-render the PDF to confirm it still returns one page (the current sheet measures 1230 against A4's 1123 before the print media block strips furniture, so there is room). Assert in interaction-check.mjs that in every medium the field's computed padding-bottom is greater than or equal to its padding-top.

biggestWin: The single thing holding this seat below 9.5 is that the two-column composition and its sticky horizon exist only at 1280 and above, so from 701 to 1279 - where most unmaximised laptop windows live - the page falls back to one 1068px track in which a moment row is drawn 73 per cent wider than it was designed, the horizon does not hold still, and at 800px of viewport height the owner and the guest both see zero of the plan on their first screen. Everything else is small beside it. What earned the 8.2: the keepsake is real now. I rendered the master at true A4, 794x1123, and it produces exactly one page with the horizon standing beside the measure at 220px and 332px, which was the 0.6 defect of round 5 and it is properly fixed rather than papered over. The space ladder is no longer a comment - driving all eleven states at four widths returns 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 26, 28, 32, 40, 48, 56 and 64 for every block margin and padding inside the field, with the only outliers being rail distances computed from days, which is exactly what a graded scale should look like. The today rule is one 344px mark at every width from 390 to 1440. And the internal craft is genuinely good where it has been looked at: the ended card's own top and bottom insets are both 81px, the guest card's left and right insets are 49 and 56 at every width, the field is symmetric in the viewport at 1440, and the two-column ratio holds 344 over 668 exactly at 1280 and 1440. What remains is not a different decision and not a rebuild. The band is one breakpoint moved from 1280 to 1000 for three properties plus two max-width declarations and three gate assertions - half a day. The centring is two lines in shell.css and one assertion, and it corrects five states at once - an hour. The column heads are one line, the sticky inset is one value, the paper margin is one value. Call the whole distance to 9.5 a day and a half of polish, all of it in b.css and shell.css, none of it touching the architecture, the palette or any adjudicated decision. The reason the score is 8.2 and not higher is that the band was named in full at round 5, the frames for it were added, and then only the easiest third of it was fixed; the hardest number in my report - zero moments above the fold on a 1279x800 laptop, on both the owner surface and the guest surface - is a number this panel already had the means to see.
